name: Jobs: completions, retries & indexed
objective: CKAD › Workloads & Scheduling. Drill the controller + batch surface: a Deployment's strategy/history, Jobs (completions/parallelism/backoffLimit/activeDeadline/ttl/Indexed), CronJobs (schedule/concurrencyPolicy/startingDeadline/history/suspend), and a no-hint parallelism diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.

questions.title: Job: completions + parallelism
questions.teach:
A **Job** runs pods to successful completion. `completions` = how many successes are needed; `parallelism` = how many run at once. A Job pod's `restartPolicy` must be `Never` or `OnFailure` (never `Always`).

**Gotcha:** the API rejects a Job whose pod `restartPolicy` is `Always`.
questions.prompt:
In `workloads-learn`, create a Job `pi` that reaches **6** successful completions running **2** at a time, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'exit 0'`, `restartPolicy: Never`.

Target: Job `pi` has completions 6, parallelism 2, restartPolicy Never.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: pi, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  completions: 6
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers: [ { name: pi, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"] } ]
YAML

verification.description: Job pi: completions 6, parallelism 2, restartPolicy Never

questions.eli5:
A **Deployment** keeps pods running *forever* (a web server). A **Job** is the opposite: it runs a task **until it finishes successfully**, then stops. Think of it like a to-do list of chores that each need to be done once, versus a shop that stays open all day.

Two dials control a Job:

- **`completions`** = "how many chores total must be done." Set 6, and the Job isn't done until 6 pods have each exited successfully.
- **`parallelism`** = "how many workers can do chores at the same time." Set 2, and at most 2 pods run concurrently, cycling through until all 6 completions are reached.

So `completions: 6, parallelism: 2` means: do 6 tasks, 2 at a time — three waves of two.

There's also a rule about what happens when a task's pod **fails**. A Job pod's **`restartPolicy`** must be `Never` (throw the pod away, start a fresh one) or `OnFailure` (restart the container in place). It can **never** be `Always` — that's for things meant to run forever, which contradicts the whole point of a Job.

**Watch out for:**

- **`restartPolicy: Always` is rejected by the API** for a Job — it must be `Never` or `OnFailure`. This lives under `spec.template.spec`, not on the Job itself.
- **`completions` = total successes needed; `parallelism` = how many at once** — don't swap them.
- **`apiVersion` is `batch/v1`, `kind: Job`** — not `v1`.
- The command `sh -c 'exit 0'` succeeds instantly, so all 6 finish fast — but each still counts as one completion.
- Without `completions`, a Job defaults to needing **one** success.
questions.deepDive:
## Job: completions + parallelism — full rundown

### Mental model
A **Job** runs pods to **successful completion** and then stops (vs a Deployment, which keeps pods running). Two knobs shape it:
- **`completions`** — total number of successful pod runs required.
- **`parallelism`** — max pods running at the same time.

The Job controller keeps launching pods, up to `parallelism` at once, until `completions` successes accumulate.

### The manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: pi
  namespace: workloads-learn
spec:
  completions: 6
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never        # REQUIRED: Never or OnFailure
      containers:
      - name: pi
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"]
```

### Field reference
| Field | Location | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `completions` | `spec` | successes needed to finish | 1 |
| `parallelism` | `spec` | max concurrent pods | 1 |
| `restartPolicy` | `spec.template.spec` | `Never` or `OnFailure` only | (must set) |
| `backoffLimit` | `spec` | retries before Failed | 6 |
| `completionMode` | `spec` | `NonIndexed` / `Indexed` | NonIndexed |

### Job patterns (completions × parallelism)
| completions | parallelism | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | single run (default) |
| N | 1 | N runs, sequential |
| N | M | N runs, up to M at once (this task: 6×2) |
| unset | M | work-queue: pods run in parallel until one signals done |

### restartPolicy — the hard rule
| Value | Valid in Job? | On pod/container failure |
|---|---|---|
| `Never` | ✅ | pod marked Failed; **new pod** created for retry |
| `OnFailure` | ✅ | **container** restarted in the same pod |
| `Always` | ❌ rejected | (Deployment-style; contradicts "run to completion") |

```
The Job "pi" is invalid: spec.template.spec.restartPolicy:
Unsupported value: "Always": supported values: "OnFailure", "Never"
```

### Imperative shortcut
```bash
kubectl create job pi --image=busybox:1.36 -- sh -c 'exit 0'
# then edit for completions/parallelism, or:
kubectl create job pi --image=busybox:1.36 --dry-run=client -o yaml -- sh -c 'exit 0' > job.yaml
```
(`kubectl create job` defaults restartPolicy to `Never` and can't set completions/parallelism directly — patch the YAML.)

### Verify
```bash
kubectl get job pi                 # COMPLETIONS 6/6
kubectl get job pi -o jsonpath='{.spec.completions}{" "}{.spec.parallelism}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.restartPolicy}'; echo
kubectl get pods -l job-name=pi
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`restartPolicy` goes under `spec.template.spec`**, not `spec` of the Job.
- **`Always` is invalid** for Jobs — a frequent trap.
- **Don't swap completions/parallelism** — completions=total, parallelism=concurrency.
- **`apiVersion: batch/v1`** (Jobs live in `batch`, not core `v1`).
- A finished Job and its pods **persist** unless you set `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` or delete them.
- `kubectl delete job` also deletes its pods (owner refs) — use `--cascade=orphan` to keep them.

### Quick reference
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: pi, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  completions: 6
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - { name: pi, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"] }
```

questions.title: Job: backoffLimit + OnFailure
questions.teach:
`backoffLimit` is how many times a Job retries a failed pod before it's marked Failed (default 6). With `restartPolicy: OnFailure` the **container** restarts in place; with `Never` a new **pod** is created per retry.

**Gotcha:** `OnFailure` restarts the container (same pod); `Never` spawns fresh pods — both count against `backoffLimit`.
questions.prompt:
In `workloads-learn`, create a Job `retry` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'exit 0'`) with `backoffLimit: 4` and `restartPolicy: OnFailure`.

Target: Job `retry` has backoffLimit 4 and pod restartPolicy OnFailure.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: retry, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      containers: [ { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"] } ]
YAML
questions.eli5:
When a Job's task fails, Kubernetes doesn't give up immediately — it retries. **`backoffLimit`** is how many times it's willing to retry before it declares the whole Job a failure and stops. The default is 6. "Backoff" means it waits a little longer between each retry (a few seconds, then more) so it doesn't hammer away instantly.

Think of it like a kid trying to unlock a door with a sticky key: they'll jiggle it a few times (`backoffLimit: 4` = four more tries), pausing a bit longer each attempt, and if it still won't open, they give up.

**How** the retry happens depends on `restartPolicy`:

- **`OnFailure`**: restart the **container in the same pod** — like the kid staying at the same door and trying again.
- **`Never`**: throw the pod away and spawn a **brand-new pod** — like walking off and coming back fresh.

Either way, **every retry counts against `backoffLimit`**.

**Watch out for:**

- **`OnFailure` restarts the container (same pod); `Never` creates fresh pods** — different mechanics, same counting toward the limit.
- **`backoffLimit` default is 6** if you don't set it.
- It counts **failures**, not successes — a Job that succeeds never touches the limit.
- The delay between retries grows (exponential backoff), capped at 6 minutes — so retries aren't instant.
- `backoffLimit` lives on the Job's `spec`; `restartPolicy` lives under `spec.template.spec`. Don't mix them up.
- Hitting the limit marks the Job **Failed** with reason `BackoffLimitExceeded`.
questions.deepDive:
## Job: backoffLimit + OnFailure — full rundown

### Mental model
When a Job's pod/container **fails**, the controller **retries** with an exponentially growing delay (backoff). `backoffLimit` caps the number of retries before the Job is marked **Failed** (`reason: BackoffLimitExceeded`). The *shape* of a retry depends on `restartPolicy`.

### The manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: retry
  namespace: workloads-learn
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"]
```

### restartPolicy: how a retry happens
| restartPolicy | Retry mechanism | Pod count | Counts toward backoffLimit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OnFailure` | **container** restarted in the **same pod** | stays 1 | ✅ yes |
| `Never` | **new pod** created each retry | grows | ✅ yes |

Both honour `backoffLimit`; they just differ in whether you see one pod restarting or many pods appearing.

### Backoff timing
Retry delay is **exponential**: ~10s, 20s, 40s … **capped at 6 minutes (360s)**. So with `Never` you'll see new pods appear with growing gaps, not instantly.

### Field placement (classic trap)
| Field | Correct location |
|---|---|
| `backoffLimit` | `spec.backoffLimit` (on the Job) |
| `restartPolicy` | `spec.template.spec.restartPolicy` (on the pod template) |
| `activeDeadlineSeconds` | `spec` (Job-level, see next lesson) |

### Related failure controls
| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `backoffLimit` | 6 | retries before Failed |
| `activeDeadlineSeconds` | unset | wall-clock cap; **overrides** backoffLimit |
| `podFailurePolicy` | unset | (1.26+) react to specific exit codes / conditions — e.g. fail fast, or ignore |

`activeDeadlineSeconds` takes precedence: if the Job runs past it, it Fails with `DeadlineExceeded` regardless of remaining retries.

### Verify
```bash
kubectl get job retry -o jsonpath='{.spec.backoffLimit}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.restartPolicy}'; echo
kubectl describe job retry        # Events show retries / backoff
kubectl get pods -l job-name=retry
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`OnFailure` = same pod, container restarts; `Never` = fresh pods.** Know the difference — a common exam question.
- **Both count toward `backoffLimit`**; it counts failures, not attempts that succeed.
- **Default `backoffLimit` is 6** when omitted.
- **Placement matters:** `backoffLimit` on the Job `spec`; `restartPolicy` on the pod template.
- **Retries are not instant** — exponential backoff up to 6 min; don't assume immediate reattempt.
- Exceeding the limit → Job `status.conditions` has `type: Failed, reason: BackoffLimitExceeded`.

### Quick reference
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: retry, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      containers:
      - { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"] }
```

questions.title: Job: deadline + auto-cleanup
questions.teach:
`activeDeadlineSeconds` caps a Job's total runtime (it's marked Failed/`DeadlineExceeded` past it). `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` auto-deletes the Job that many seconds after it finishes.

**Gotcha:** `activeDeadlineSeconds` bounds wall-clock time and overrides `backoffLimit`; `ttl` cleanup starts only once the Job has completed/failed.
questions.prompt:
In `workloads-learn`, create a Job `bounded` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'sleep 3600'`, `restartPolicy: Never`) with `activeDeadlineSeconds: 300` and `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 30`.

Target: Job `bounded` has activeDeadlineSeconds 300 and ttlSecondsAfterFinished 30.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: bounded, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 300
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 30
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers: [ { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"] } ]
YAML
questions.eli5:
Two timers can be attached to a Job, and they do different things.

**`activeDeadlineSeconds`** is a stopwatch on the whole Job: "you have 300 seconds total to finish — go over and I pull the plug." If the task is still running when time's up, the Job is marked **Failed** with the reason `DeadlineExceeded`. It's like a kitchen timer during an exam: pencils down when it rings, no matter how many retries you had left.

**`ttlSecondsAfterFinished`** is a clean-up timer that only starts **after** the Job has finished (succeeded or failed): "30 seconds after you're done, I'll throw you in the bin." It auto-deletes the finished Job (and its pods) so they don't pile up as clutter.

In this task the command is `sleep 3600` (an hour), but the deadline is 300 seconds — so the Job will actually hit the deadline and fail, then get cleaned up 30 seconds later.

**Watch out for:**

- **`activeDeadlineSeconds` is wall-clock time and OVERRIDES `backoffLimit`.** Once the deadline passes, the Job fails immediately even if it had retries left.
- **`ttlSecondsAfterFinished` only starts counting once the Job has completed or failed** — not from when it was created. A Job that never finishes is never TTL-cleaned.
- Both fields live on the **Job's `spec`**, not the pod template.
- TTL cleanup deletes the Job **and its pods** — grab logs before they vanish.
- `activeDeadlineSeconds` measures time the Job is *active*; it's about elapsed wall-clock, not CPU time.
questions.deepDive:
## Job: deadline + auto-cleanup — full rundown

### Mental model
Two independent timers:
- **`activeDeadlineSeconds`** — a hard **wall-clock cap** on how long the Job may run. Exceed it → Job **Failed** with `reason: DeadlineExceeded`; running pods are terminated. It **overrides `backoffLimit`**.
- **`ttlSecondsAfterFinished`** — a **cleanup** timer that starts only **after** the Job reaches Complete/Failed, then auto-deletes the Job (and its owned pods).

### The manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: bounded
  namespace: workloads-learn
spec:
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 300       # kill the Job after 300s of wall-clock
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 30      # delete 30s after it finishes
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
```
Here `sleep 3600` would run an hour, but `activeDeadlineSeconds: 300` forces failure at 5 minutes; TTL then removes it 30s later.

### Field comparison
| Field | Clock starts | Trigger | Effect | Overrides |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `activeDeadlineSeconds` | when Job becomes **active** | elapsed > value | Job → Failed (`DeadlineExceeded`), pods terminated | **beats `backoffLimit`** |
| `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` | when Job **finishes** (Complete/Failed) | elapsed > value after finish | Job + pods **deleted** | — |

Both are on `spec` (Job-level), **not** the pod template.

### activeDeadlineSeconds: Job-level vs pod-level
- `spec.activeDeadlineSeconds` — bounds the **whole Job**.
- `spec.template.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds` — bounds **each pod** individually (a different field!). Don't confuse them; the task wants the Job-level one.

### TTL controller behaviour
- Requires the **TTLAfterFinished** controller (GA since 1.23; on by default).
- Counts from the completion time, not creation. A Job that never finishes is **never** TTL-cleaned.
- Deletes the Job object; owned pods are garbage-collected with it. **Grab logs first** if you need them.
- `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 0` deletes immediately upon finishing.

### Verify
```bash
kubectl get job bounded \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds}{" "}{.spec.ttlSecondsAfterFinished}'; echo   # 300 30
kubectl describe job bounded     # watch for DeadlineExceeded
# after it fails + 30s:
kubectl get job bounded          # NotFound (TTL-deleted)
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`activeDeadlineSeconds` overrides `backoffLimit`** — once the deadline hits, retries left don't matter; Job Fails.
- **TTL starts at finish, not creation** — an unfinished Job lingers forever.
- **Both fields on the Job `spec`**, not under `template`. (And beware the separate pod-level `activeDeadlineSeconds`.)
- **TTL deletes pods too** → logs disappear; collect them before cleanup.
- `DeadlineExceeded` is wall-clock, not CPU seconds.
- Failure reason to recognize: `status.conditions[].reason: DeadlineExceeded`.

### Quick reference
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: bounded, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 300
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 30
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"] }
```

questions.title: Indexed Job
questions.teach:
`completionMode: Indexed` gives each of the `completions` pods a unique index (0..N-1) in `$JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX` — for partitioned/parallel work where each worker handles its slice.

**Gotcha:** default `completionMode` is `NonIndexed`; Indexed needs `completions` set and each index must succeed once.
questions.prompt:
In `workloads-learn`, create an **Indexed** Job `indexed` (`completionMode: Indexed`) with `completions: 4`, `parallelism: 2`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'exit 0'`, `restartPolicy: Never`.

Target: Job `indexed` has completionMode Indexed, completions 4, parallelism 2.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: indexed, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  completionMode: Indexed
  completions: 4
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers: [ { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"] } ]
YAML

verification.description: Job indexed: completionMode Indexed, completions 4, parallelism 2

questions.eli5:
Imagine you have a big job split into numbered chunks — "process file 0, file 1, file 2, file 3." You want four workers, but each one needs to know *which* chunk is theirs so they don't all grab the same file.

A normal (NonIndexed) Job treats its pods as interchangeable — any pod can do any unit of work, and they don't get numbers. That's fine for identical tasks, but useless when each worker needs a distinct slice.

**`completionMode: Indexed`** fixes this. It hands each pod a unique number from 0 to N-1 (where N is `completions`). The pod reads its number from the environment variable **`$JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX`**. So pod "index 2" knows to go process file 2. Each index must succeed exactly once for the Job to be complete.

Here: `completions: 4` means indices 0, 1, 2, 3; `parallelism: 2` means two run at a time.

It's like numbered lockers at a pool — four lockers, two attendants working at once, and each locker gets opened exactly once by whoever's assigned its number.

**Watch out for:**

- **The default `completionMode` is `NonIndexed`** — you must explicitly set `Indexed` to get the numbering.
- **Indexed requires `completions` to be set** — the number of indices comes from it (0..completions-1).
- **Each index must succeed once**; the index is exposed as the env var `$JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX` (and in the pod's annotation/hostname).
- `completionMode` lives on the Job's `spec`, alongside `completions` and `parallelism`.
- `parallelism` still just limits concurrency — it doesn't change which indices exist.
questions.deepDive:
## Indexed Job — full rundown

### Mental model
By default a Job is **NonIndexed**: pods are interchangeable and any pod can satisfy any completion. An **Indexed** Job assigns each pod a stable **completion index** `0..(completions-1)`, so each pod knows which **slice** of partitioned work it owns — ideal for static work partitioning across parallel workers.

### The manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: indexed
  namespace: workloads-learn
spec:
  completionMode: Indexed      # default is NonIndexed
  completions: 4               # → indices 0,1,2,3
  parallelism: 2               # 2 at a time
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"]
```

### completionMode
| Mode | Pods | Index? | Completion rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NonIndexed` (default) | interchangeable | none | any `completions` successes finish it |
| `Indexed` | each owns an index | 0..N-1 | **each index** must succeed exactly once |

### How a pod learns its index
The index is exposed three ways:
| Mechanism | Where | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Env var | `$JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX` | `2` |
| Pod annotation | `batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index` | `2` |
| Pod name / hostname suffix | `<job>-<index>-<rand>` | `indexed-2-abcde` |

```bash
# typical usage inside the container
echo "I am worker $JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX"
```

### Requirements & rules
- **`completions` must be set** (and > 0) — it defines the index range.
- **`parallelism`** limits concurrency only; it doesn't change which indices exist.
- Each index runs until it has **one success**; a failed index is retried (subject to `backoffLimit`).
- Works with `backoffLimit`, `activeDeadlineSeconds`, `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` as usual.
- `backoffLimitPerIndex` (1.28+, beta) can cap retries **per index** instead of globally.

### Verify
```bash
kubectl get job indexed -o jsonpath='{.spec.completionMode}{" "}{.spec.completions}{" "}{.spec.parallelism}'; echo
# → Indexed 4 2
kubectl get pods -l job-name=indexed \
  -o custom-columns=POD:.metadata.name,INDEX:.metadata.annotations.batch\\.kubernetes\\.io/job-completion-index
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Default is `NonIndexed`** — you must spell out `completionMode: Indexed`.
- **`completions` is mandatory** for Indexed; without it the Job is invalid.
- **Each index must succeed once** — it's not "any N successes" like NonIndexed.
- The index env var is exactly **`JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX`** — memorize the name.
- `completionMode` lives on the Job `spec`, beside `completions`/`parallelism` — not in the template.
- Indexed mode is how you do static partitioning (e.g. shard files by index); pair with `parallelism` for throughput.

### Quick reference
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: indexed, namespace: workloads-learn }
spec:
  completionMode: Indexed
  completions: 4
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sh","-c","exit 0"] }
```
